advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile find_similar's 'Never raises' docstring with its Exception-only (not BaseException) handling, or state the intentional interrupt-propagation carve-out.
evidence: src/rebar/similar/catchup.py:212: `    except BaseException:` then `raise` re-raises KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit out of _apply
advisory.finding: find_similar documents 'Never raises' but only catches Exception, so a BaseException (e.g. KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit) raised from inside catch_up/_apply — which itself re-raises BaseException after ROLLBACK — will propagate past find_similar to the caller on the ticket-create write path.
scenarios: Operator sends SIGINT while a large catch-up reconcile is running during a ticket create

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'sqlite lacks FTS5' from file corruption in open_index so a permanent capability gap is not masked as a transient rebuild loop.
evidence: src/rebar/similar/index.py: `conn.execute(f"CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS docs USING fts5({_FTS_COLUMNS})")`
src/rebar/similar/index.py:132: `except (sqlite3.DatabaseError, StaleIndex) as exc:` catches the missing-FTS5 error, _discard, then retry fails the same way → None
ABSENCE: no distinct detection/message for 'FTS5 unavailable in this sqlite build' vs a corrupt file
advisory.finding: When the sqlite build lacks FTS5, `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5` raises sqlite3.OperationalError (a DatabaseError); open_index discards and retries, fails identically, and returns None — so retrieval degrades to permanently-empty results with only a per-call warning, indistinguishable at the call site from 'index consulted and matched nothing'.
scenarios: Python linked against a system sqlite compiled without the FTS5 extension

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs catch_up twice after an index-producing reduce_ticket run and asserts the second run re-hashes with indexed==0 and a subsequent run has an empty diff (convergence), covering catchup.py's documented one-run-of-lag contract.
evidence: catchup.py docstring: 'One run of lag is expected after any run that indexed something. Re-indexing calls the reducer, which writes a ``.cache.json`` into the ticket directory, and that write lands AFTER ``live_entries`` read the mtime now persisted in ``dirstate``. The next catch-up therefore sees a moved mtime ... re-hashes them; the hash is unchanged, so nothing is re-indexed and the stored mtime converges. The run after that is fully warm.'

ABSENCE: no test in test_similar_tickets_index.py or test_similar_tickets_scale.py runs catch_up twice after an index-producing run and asserts that the second run re-hashes but indexes 0 while the third run is fully warm (empty diff). test_catch_up_does_no_work_on_an_unchanged_store only runs catch_up once after _indexed(), so it never observes the post-index .cache.json write-back and convergence sequence the contract describes.
advisory.finding: The documented 'one run of lag then convergence' catch-up behavior is untested. catchup.py's docstring states that after any run that indexed something, re-indexing writes a .cache.json into the ticket directory AFTER live_entries read the mtime, so the NEXT catch-up re-hashes those exact directories (hash unchanged, nothing re-indexed) and the stored mtime converges, the run after that being fully warm. No test drives this sequence: a regression where catch-up re-indexes the same directories on every run (never converging / index thrash) would pass all existing tests, since test_catch_up_does_no_work_on_an_unchanged_store writes tickets via direct event files (no reducer .cache.json write-back) rather than exercising the reduce_ticket-produces-a-cache-write-back path the convergence contract describes.
scenarios: A regression in the mtime write-back / convergence logic causing catch-up to re-index the same directories on every read (permanent thrash), silently blowing the warm-path latency budget the design depends on.
